commit.message:
feat(responses): add WebSocket lane overflow isolation (#4225)

A slow WebSocket lane currently closes the managed session when its
event queue fills. Add `isolate_lane_overflow=True` to the sync and
async session constructors. With this option, healthy lanes keep using
the same connection. The default remains `False`.

Failed lanes discard queued events and collected response state. Reads
keep raising the first buffer error. Their IDs stay reserved until
reconnect. The guide explains how the session frees space when its
queues fill. It also explains which events become unavailable when the
default lane fails. Physical connection failures still end the session.
This uses the existing router and reader, without new limits or
dependencies.

Validation: all 200 focused session cases pass on Python 3.10/Pydantic 1
and Python 3.13/Pydantic 2. They cover both policies, all queue budgets,
eviction, cached finals, default routing, transport failure and
reconnect. Pinned Ruff, format and ty checks pass.

Co-authored-by: markstuart-oai <323302876+markstuart-oai@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
feat(responses): accumulate rich WebSocket progress (#4224)

`ResponsesWebSocketAccumulator` now tracks reasoning, shell, interpreter
and tool status progress, plus queued response metadata. Status
accumulation covers code interpreter, file/web search, image generation
and MCP calls. `detailed_snapshot()` exposes these observations;
terminal responses remain authoritative.

Shell observations use indexed command facts. Done events retain every
output row for their command, including empty arrays, outcomes and
metadata. Whole-item output stays authoritative without guessing command
boundaries or inventing outcomes. The helper buffers fragments and
indexes command counts by call ID, avoiding repeated scans of retained
output.

Detailed full items retain omitted, null and present ID fields. Function
and custom tool records that omit ID bind their first matching progress
ID; explicit-null, present-ID and unscaffolded replacement policies
remain compatible.

Validation: focused accumulator checks pass with Python 3.10/Pydantic v1
and Python 3.13/Pydantic v2. Ruff, formatting and ty pass. Regressions
cover all 28 rich progress/status tags, reasoning parts, queued refresh,
sparse shell observations, full completion arrays, metadata presence and
identity guards.

---------

Co-authored-by: markstuart-oai <323302876+markstuart-oai@users.noreply.github.com>

fix(api): preserve Responses WebSocket connection behavior (#4221)

Use the SDK-owned connection helpers for stable and beta Responses
WebSockets. This keeps header overrides, connection defaults, cleanup
and recovery behavior in place when the clients are regenerated. It
removes duplicate connection policy code from both generated resources.

Validation: 617 targeted tests and 10 retained exit tests pass against a
fresh, noneditable wheel installation. Two normal generation runs
produce identical code. The three SDK-owned test updates are included in
this PR.

commit.message:
fix(realtime): validate beta WebSocket authentication profiles (#4218)

A bare workload-identity or Bedrock client could attempt a beta Realtime
handshake without applying its configured authentication. Reject those
unsupported profiles locally before credential refresh or connection,
and enforce the documented X.509 WebSocket exclusion.

Preserve explicit `Authorization` settings for other clients, including
default and connection headers, case-insensitive overrides, and removal
with `omit`. Document this compatibility boundary without adding
provider token exchange or signing.

Validation:
- Before the change: 8 refusal cases failed and 16 explicit-header
compatibility cases passed.
- After the change: all 24 profile tests passed.
- All 74 focused tests passed, including existing beta Azure and
redirect controls; the same 74 passed against a locally built,
non-editable wheel.
- Ruff formatting, lint, and diff checks passed.

---------

commit.message:
refactor(websocket): add SDK-owned Responses policy helpers (#4219)

Add private SDK-owned helpers for Responses WebSocket setup, iteration,
progress tracking, and cleanup. Focused sync and async tests cover
prepared headers, argument collisions, generator controls, retry
progress, and cleanup error precedence.

Existing public managers do not yet call these helpers. Rollout needs
three steps: merge this helper change into public main, land compiler
delegation, then regenerate and promote the bindings. The compiler must
wait for the merged helper change; an open PR is insufficient. The first
dependency needs no package release.

Validation: 585 focused WebSocket tests passed, including the 18 new
helper cases. Ruff formatting and lint, plus ty 0.0.87 checks for both
changed files, passed.

---------
